doc.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Lee Morgan teasing Dizzy Gillespie over the phone
summary: At dinner at Morgan's Bronx home, Morgan joked that Gillespie was trying to steal his drummer, and Gillespie replied not to come down to get bruised.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: Tell us about working with Lee Morgan.

Oh that was beautiful man. Now there is, I got a funny story to tell you about Lee Morgan. When I was working with Lee Morgan, I was invited to his house for dinner one night, when him and Helen was together you know? And they lived in the Bronx, not far from Yankee Stadium. So we’re sitting there having dinner and all this, before, Lee Morgan, I mean Dizzy Gillespie and Art they would come and we’d play in Slug’s quite a bit this club in the lower part of New York. So we’re sitting having dinner and the

phone rings you know? So I don’t know who it was on the other end, because Lee was talking on the phone. So I heard him say, “man I know why you’re coming ‘round all the time man, because you’re trying to steal my drummer.” And Dizzy was working at the Vanguard you know with his band. So Lee said, “just for that man, I ought to come down there and burn on you. I’ll bring my horn down there and burn on you old man.” And there was a pause, and then all of a sudden, Lee Morgan just broke out laughing. I mean he was hysterical laughing. So we’re trying to find out what Dizzy said. So I said, “what did Dizzy say, man?” So he say what Dizzy say, “don’t come down here to get bruised.” But I’ll tell you Dizzy, all the trumpet players called Dizzy Gillespie the king. I mean he is the king on that trumpet. There’s nobody can play that trumpet like Dizzy Gillespie. And you know, and so Lee was teasing, you know so he say “well don’t come down here to get bruised.”
